why: What an agent transaction carries, written once and read by two implementations: the Rust law `app::agent_lane_preview_tests` (`🧪️tests/🤖️agent-lane-preview/🦀️.rs`) decodes each case's host effects from their wire form (the kernel `Effect`'s camelCase JSON) and asks `agent_lane_uncarried_lanes` — the check the agent lane's preview (`preview_addressed_action`, the MCP gateway's `action_prepare`) runs on every previewed completion — and the AJV twin (`🧪️tests/🤖️agent-lane-preview/🟦️.ts`) derives the same answer with one JSON Schema per lane. An agent transaction carries only a command's document, config, draft and owned-child operations; the agent lane fails closed on everything else. A `publication` states how many operations the transaction carries (`carriedOps`: document, config and draft ops and owned-child groups), lists the host effects the previewed command requests and how many items each other lane holds (window-config ops, extension calls, app events, selection writes, follow-up tasks, and the presence, transient and window-transient mutations of the app's ephemeral hook and of the job's completion). `uncarried` names every lane that is not empty, each once, in `lanes` order: a load-document effect is a whole-document replacement; a media, icon or video export a file download; a file or media-frame request a file request; a guest-emitted interaction verb (a dispatch-action or replay-shell-command effect naming `interactionSelect`, `interactionHover`, `clearSelection`, `selectAll`, `setSelectionMode` or `setInteractionGranularity`) a selection change; any other dispatch-action effect a follow-up dispatch; an open-dialog effect a dialog; a notify effect a notice; a clipboard write a clipboard write; opening or closing a window, a panel, navigation, an external URL, spawning or opening a plugin instance, switching the active utility or tool and replaying a shell command a shell change; an extension invocation (as an effect or through the extension lane) extension calls; every other host effect a host request. The `presentation` lanes (a notice, selection changes) only present the result to the human who ran the command: beside carried operations they are omitted, on their own (`carriedOps` 0) they are the command's whole effect and are named like every other lane. The `verdict`: `carried` when `uncarried` is empty (the only answer the preview settles on); `noEffect` when nothing is carried and `uncarried` names presentation lanes only — the command changes nothing in this state and is refused `app.command.no-effect` with the app's own notice; `uncarried` otherwise — refused `interactive-job.agent-lane-uncarried` naming those lanes. So an agent is never told "done" for a verb whose shell run acts where its transaction would do nothing.

cases.name: a publication of document, config, draft and child operations only is carried
a follow-up dispatch is refused, not dropped
a notice alone is the command's whole effect and is refused as no effect
shell changes of every kind share one lane named once
a download and a sync request are named in lane order
extension calls count once whether effect or lane
selection writes, app events and window-config operations are refused
a notice beside carried operations is omitted
selecting what the command made beside carried operations is omitted
a follow-up dispatch beside carried operations is still refused
selecting without carrying anything changes nothing and is refused as no effect
a notice beside a follow-up dispatch without carried operations is uncarried, not no effect
selecting what the command made through a dispatched interaction verb beside carried operations is omitted
a replayed interaction verb without carried operations changes nothing
